(post may be null).  A prohibition counts one violation for every step whose label (including events occurring at
that step) satisfies the condition.  An obligation becomes pending at any step satisfying the trigger ("START" =
pending from the beginning) and is fulfilled by a later (or the same) step satisfying the discharge; it can be
triggered again; it is violated if it is still pending when the trajectory ends.

parsed.text: A shopper who starts a trip is obliged to return the cart to the cart corral at the top-left before leaving.
It is forbidden to leave a cart anywhere except the designated cart corral at cell (0,1).
It is forbidden to pick up shelf items unless the shopper currently has a cart.
At the beginning of the trip, the shopper is obliged to take the entrance cart before doing the shopping.
It is forbidden to exit the supermarket unless the cart has already been returned to the cart corral.
Item pickup interactions are allowed only at recognized product access cells, treating the upper and lower aisle sides of the same shelf as equivalent.
All interactions must occur at service points: the entrance cart bay, the return corral, or one of the recognized product access cells.
After the cart has been returned to the corral, the shopper must not perform any further interactions before exiting.

Every action costs the same, so demonstrators prefer short trajectories -- unless an unknown social norm makes them behave otherwise. Your task is to propose candidate norms (obligations or prohibitions) that could explain the demonstrated behaviour.
Each demonstration is listed step by step as  `k: {atoms true in the state} action`.

Available atoms:
- at(x,y) -- the agent is at cell (x,y); x = column (0 = left), y = row (0 = top); N decreases y, S increases y, E increases x, W decreases x
- actions N, S, E, W, MOVE (any of the four moves), INTERACT (any interaction with an object: the different kinds of interaction are NOT distinguished), EXIT (leave the store; always the last action)
- hasCart -- the agent is holding/pushing a shopping cart
- cartAt(x,y) -- the cart is parked (or stationed) at cell (x,y)
- handFull -- the agent carries an item by hand
- actions PICKUP_CART, LEAVE_CART (put the cart down on the current cell), PICKUP_ITEM (take an item from an adjacent shelf); each of these is also an INTERACT

The demonstrations are now shown in a lower-level representation that exposes distinctions hidden before (newly available: cart_possession, cart_location, hand, actions_primitive). Identify the hidden distinctions and use them to define higher-level state properties and/or events (in "abstraction"), possibly hierarchically, and propose norms expressed over them. Norms may also use the primitive atoms directly.
Propose 8 diverse candidate hypotheses.

Output format: return ONLY a JSON list (no prose, no code fences). Each element:
{"id": short_name, "text": one-sentence natural-language statement of the norm,
 "abstraction": {"state_properties": {name: FORMULA, ...},
                 "events": {name: {"pre": FORMULA, "post": FORMULA or null}, ...}},
 "norm": {"type": "prohibition", "condition": FORMULA}
       | {"type": "obligation", "trigger": FORMULA or "START", "discharge": FORMULA}}
FORMULA := atom | name of a property/event defined in this hypothesis | {"not": F} | {"and": [F, ...]}
         | {"or": [F, ...]} | {"le"|"lt"|"ge"|"gt"|"eq": [numeric_feature, integer]}
Semantics.  A trajectory is a sequence of steps (state s_k, action a_k).  A step's label contains the atoms true in
s_k and the action a_k.  A state property is a formula over state atoms (no actions).  An event
{"pre": P, "post": Q} occurs at step k when P holds for the label of step k and Q holds in the next state s_{k+1}
(post may be null).  A prohibition counts one violation for every step whose label (including events occurring at
that step) satisfies the condition.  An obligation becomes pending at any step satisfying the trigger ("START" =
pending from the beginning) and is fulfilled by a later (or the same) step satisfying the discharge; it can be
triggered again; it is violated if it is still pending when the trajectory ends.

parsed.text: A shopper who starts a trip is obliged to return the cart to the cart corral at the top-left before leaving.
It is forbidden to leave a cart anywhere except the designated cart corral at cell (0,1).
It is forbidden to pick up shelf items unless the shopper currently has a cart.
At the beginning of the trip, the shopper is obliged to take the entrance cart before doing the shopping.
It is forbidden to exit the supermarket unless the cart has already been returned to the cart corral.
Item pickup interactions are allowed only at recognized product access cells, treating the upper and lower aisle sides of the same shelf as equivalent.
All interactions must occur at service points: the entrance cart bay, the return corral, or one of the recognized product access cells.
After the cart has been returned to the corral, the shopper must not perform any further interactions before exiting.

accepted.description: [g1_return_cart_to_corral] OBLIGED: after start, eventually return_cart_to_corral (before exit)  where cart_corral_cell := at(0,1); cart_returned := cartAt(0,1); return_cart_to_corral := (cart_corral_cell ∧ hasCart ∧ LEAVE_CART) · cart_returned

[g1_must_take_entrance_cart] OBLIGED: after start, eventually take_entrance_cart (before exit)  where entrance_cart_cell := (at(1,5) ∧ cartAt(1,5)); take_entrance_cart := (entrance_cart_cell ∧ PICKUP_CART) · hasCart

[g1_item_pickups_at_product_access_cells] FORBIDDEN: (PICKUP_ITEM ∧ ¬product_access)  where apple_access := at(1,3); bread_access := (at(3,4) ∨ at(3,2)); eggs_access := (at(6,4) ∨ at(6,2)); milk_access := (at(5,4) ∨ at(5,2)); product_access := (bread_access ∨ milk_access ∨ eggs_access ∨ apple_access); pickup_at_product_access := (PICKUP_ITEM ∧ product_access)

[g1_interactions_only_at_service_points] FORBIDDEN: (INTERACT ∧ ¬service_point)  where apple_access := at(1,3); bread_access := (at(3,4) ∨ at(3,2)); eggs_access := (at(6,4) ∨ at(6,2)); entrance_cart_bay := at(1,5); milk_access := (at(5,4) ∨ at(5,2)); product_access := (bread_access ∨ milk_access ∨ eggs_access ∨ apple_access); return_corral := at(0,1); service_point := (entrance_cart_bay ∨ return_corral ∨ product_access)
